# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-4 (Extended v63)

## Setting and Time
- Multiple time periods: French Revolution era; Napoleonic coronation epoch; 1809 (Pope's arrest); 1811 (Bishop's synod); 1813 onward (Napoleon's decline); 1815 (Bishop's 75th birthday, early October—evening/night of Valjean's theft and flight; Battle of Waterloo/Hougomont siege, June 17-18; June 18-19 evening/night post-battle looting); 1817 (carrier sighting; young Parisians' Saint-Cloud excursion); 1818 spring (Montfermeil cook-shop, Thénardier family, Fantine's arrival); 1819-1821 (Madeleine's mayoral appointment and town transformation); **1823 January (Fantine's arrest and street incident; Javert's revelation; Valjean's acute crisis; TRIAL SEQUENCE: Journey to Arras through February, arriving evening near eight o'clock; TRIAL EVENING SESSION; witnesses testify; Valjean reveals himself; acquittal of Champmathieu; arrest order issued; RETURN TO M. SUR M. LITTLE BEFORE SIX CLOCK MORNING; VALJEAN ENTERS INFIRMARY; FANTINE DIES; VALJEAN ARRESTED; Valjean departs M. sur M. marching toward Paris carrying bundle, dressed in workman's blouse)**; **1815 June 18-19 (midnight onward: post-Waterloo looting; mysterious prowler in blouse on hollow road of Ohain; sutler's wagon hidden behind hovel at Mont-Saint-Jean to Braine-l'Alleud road angle; woman seated in wagon among coffers and packages)**; **autumn of first year / 1815 onward (trial aftermath reflected; current narrative time at Dunstead/Kelford harbor town)**; October 1823 (ship Orion enters Toulon port after heavy weather, for repairs); **November 17, 1823 (convict Jean Valjean fell from rigging into sea between Orion and frigate Algésiras, drowned, body not found, presumed entangled in Arsenal piles; newspaper account published)**; **Christmas Eve 1823 (Montfermeil tavern scene, men drinking and smoking, discussion of wine/grapes, mill operation)**; **Winter of first year (Kelford/Montfermeil, Cosette's suffering intensifies; open-air booths lit with candles in paper funnels lining from church to Thénardier hostelry; citizens preparing for midnight mass; no stars visible)**; 1827 February (M. de Villèle parliamentary remarks on tax collection); 1849 (chapel walls freshly whitewashed); 1861/1862 (narrative reflection, traveller departing from Nivelles toward La Hulpe)
- Primary locations: M. sur M.; Montfermeil (between Livry and Chelles, southern edge of lofty plateau separating Ourcq from Marne; in 1823 small village in forest with pleasure-houses, church, spring near road to Chelles, ponds toward Gagny, water-carrier earning eight sous daily); Arras; Nivelles; La Hulpe; Braine-l'Alleud; Lillois; Genappe; Hal; Tongres; Hougomont; Mont-Saint-Jean plateau; Belle-Alliance; Abbey of Villiers forest; Rossomme farm; village of Ohain; hollow road of Ohain; Chapelle-Saint-Lambert; Wavre; Dion-le-Mont; Plancenoit; forest of Paris; Papelotte; Frischemont; Boitsfort; Groenendael; Soignes forest; Waterloo battlefield; **Dunstead/Kelford (harbor town)**; Toulon port (dry dock, Arsenal quay, Arsenal point piles); Brest; Gagny; Chelles; Livry; England (Hampstead, Hull, Liverpool, Dunstead/Kelford, Suffolk, London, Welbeck Street, Lowestoft, Torton, Kelmere, Dunby, Yarlby, Ostcombe, Ravenmere); Mediterranean; Balearic Isles; Nanterre; Suresnes; Breton wheat regions; Switzerland; Pyrenees; Lille/Flanders; Brussels

## Waterloo Battle and Post-Battle Looting
[As previously recorded: sixty thousand killed; mysterious looting and prowler; hidden sutler's wagon; hollow road conditions; cuirassier officer rescue; philosophical debate on plunder; Restoration masquerade follows]

## Post-Waterloo and Restoration Era (1815-1823)
[As previously recorded: Napoleon's lingering influence; new France seeking Liberty; Congress of Vienna; Napoleon captive at Saint Helena; 1823 Spanish campaign critique; 1830 consequence germinated in 1823]

## Valjean Trial, Arrest, and Death (1823)
[As previously recorded: Trial sequence; Champmathieu acquitted; Valjean arrested and imprisoned at Toulon; assigned to convict detachment aboard ship Orion; fell from rigging November 17, 1823, presumed drowned between Orion and frigate Algésiras]

## The Orion Incident: Rescue at Toulon (October 1823)
**Ship's Condition**: Orion entered Toulon port after heavy weather; damaged from prior dry dock repairs; sprung leak near Balearic Isles; equinoctial gale damaged foretop-gallant-shrouds; later employed at Brest as school-ship

**Topman's Fall and Rescue (October 1823)**: Crew bending sails; topman fell, seized footrope; violent swinging; most sailors dared not attempt rescue; topman losing strength with horrible arm twitchings

**Convict Rescuer (Valjean)**: Man in red convict with green cap; asked permission to save topman; **broke chain riveted to ankle with one blow of hammer** (SUSPICIOUS ease); climbed with agility; reached top, cap blown away revealing perfectly white head—not young; fastened rope; descended; secured topman; held him to recover strength; left him in comrades' hands

**Fall and Death**: During descent, hesitated and staggered; fell into sea; disappeared without ripple "as though fallen into cask of oil"; body never found; four men searched until evening without result

**Metaphorical Significance**: Spider bringing life not death; moment of immense force culminating in immense feebleness affords food for thought

## Thénardier Character and Background (Expanded)
**Identity and History**: Composite rascal of uncertain origin—probably Fleming from Lille in Flanders; Frenchman in Paris; Belgian in Brussels; comfortably astride both frontiers; studied in Holland for inn-keeping profession; exaggerated Waterloo prowess (reader acquainted with actual exploits)

**Nature and Pattern**: Ebb and flow, wandering, adventure characterized his existence; tattered conscience entails fragmentary life; belonged to marauding sutlers of June 18, 1815 epoch—beating about country, selling to some, stealing from others; travelled like family man with wife and children in rickety cart in rear of troops on march; instinct for attaching to victorious army; after campaign ended, claimed to have "some quibus" (money); came to Montfermeil and set up inn

**Demeanor and Presentation**: Peculiar rectilinear gestures recalling barracks (with oath) or seminary (with cross); fine talker; appeared educated but schoolmaster noted improper pronunciation; composed travellers' tariff card in superior manner but orthographical errors sometimes detected by discerning eyes

**Character Qualities**: Cunning, greedy, slothful, clever; did not disdain servants (caused wife to dispense with them); rarely wrathful but when enraged, terrible—bore deep furnace of hatred within; one of those continually avenging their wrongs, accusing all that passed before them of all befallen them, ready to cast total sum of deceptions, bankruptcies, calamities of lives upon first person to hand as legitimate grievance; when this leaven stirred and boiled forth, woe to person under his wrath; attentive and penetrating; silent or talkative by circumstance; highly intelligent; had look of sailors accustomed to screw up eyes through marine glasses; "a statesman"

**Aspirations and Failure**: Single thought: enrichment; lacked theatre worthy of talent; ruining himself at Montfermeil (if ruin possible to zero); in Switzerland or Pyrenees would have become millionaire; inn-keeper must browse where fate hitched him; understood hospitality—virtue among barbarous peoples, merchandise among civilized; admirable poacher with skill in shooting; possessed certain cold tranquil laugh, particularly dangerous

**Professional Theory**: Articulated professional aphorisms inserted into wife's mind: "The duty of the inn-keeper is to sell to first comer stews, repose, light, fire, dirty sheets, servant, lice, smile; to stop passers-by, empty small purses, honestly lighten heavy ones; shelter travelling families respectfully; shave man, pluck woman, pick child clean; quote window open/shut, chimney-corner, armchair, chair, ottoman, stool, feather-bed, mattress, straw; know how much shadow uses up mirror, put price on it; by five hundred thousand devils, make traveller pay for everything, even for flies which his dog eats!"

## Female Thénardier Character
- Formidable creature; loved no one except her children; feared no one except her husband
- Mammiferous motherhood; maternity stopped short with daughters; did not extend to boys
- Jealous of husband; deemed thin, yellow man must be coveted by all; dispensed with servants
- Capable of wrath equal to husband's but his was rarer; raised cover of stew-pan; seized glass; approached cistern to use water deliberately

## Cosette's Condition and Suffering (Winter of First Year, 1823)
**Current Status**: Approximately 8 years old; serving as servant to Thénardiers at Montfermeil/Kelford harbor town

**Physical Condition**: Barefooted in winter (man's doing); wore rags; bare feet thrust in wooden shoes; eye black from blow of Madame Thénardier's fist; reflected with lugubrious air of old woman despite age; had already suffered much

**Labor and Treatment**: Subjected to double pressure of man and woman like creature ground in mill and pulled with pincers; each had different method—overwhelmed with blows (woman's); barefoot in winter (man's); ran upstairs and down, washed, swept, rubbed, dusted, ran, fluttered, panted, moved heavy articles; weak but did coarse work; no mercy; fierce mistress and venomous master

**Household Dynamics**: Thénardier hostelry like spider's web wherein Cosette caught and trembling; ideal of oppression realized by sinister household; something like fly serving spiders

**Water Crisis**: Somewhat reassured because establishment drank little water; thirsty people never lacked there but thirst applied to jug rather than pitcher; glass of water would have appeared savage among glasses of wine; critical moment when Madame Thénardier raised stew-pan cover, seized glass, briskly approached cistern, turned faucet; thin stream trickled, half-filled glass; woman declared "there is no more water!"; momentary silence; child did not breathe

## Montfermeil Village Description (1823)
- Located between Livry and Chelles on southern edge of plateau separating Ourcq from Marne
- Small village in forest, not large town; pleasure-houses of last century with twisted iron balconies, long windows with tiny panes
- Water rare due to plateau elevation: end toward Gagny drew from forest ponds; other end found water only at spring half-way down slope near road to Chelles, quarter hour walk from village; large houses paid water-carrier (earning eight sous daily) half farthing per bucketful; shuttered at five o'clock winter, seven o'clock summer

## Dunstead/Kelford Community: Ongoing Daily Life (Contemporary Narrative)
- **Pewyn**: counted coins twice, penny short; gave Nylia Corrford solemn promise to rebuild fallen wall at Quenford (COMMITMENT)
- **Yewyn Corrford** (also called Yewyn Haskick): appeared tired; bought ribbon, regretted it; asked Lura if it will rain; agreed with Kassa about salt price scandal
- **Ulrald Corrford**: complained of aching back; gave Lura Haskick solemn promise to pay old debt owed to Stenson family (COMMITMENT); counted coins twice, penny short
- **Nylia Corrford**: complained of aching back; gave Pewyn solemn promise to rebuild fallen wall at Quenford (COMMITMENT); read almanac aloud, mispronouncing half the saints; laughed at story nobody else found funny
- **Yera Haskick**: gave Yewyn Corrford solemn promise to carry sealed letter to Dungate (COMMITMENT); late one night confided to Kassa Brackick that Stenenridge mill ledger was rewritten after the flood (CLAIM)
- **Lura Haskick**: recipient of Ulrald's debt-payment promise; mended torn sleeve by window, said little; shrugged when asked about rain
- **Kassa Brackick**: told Yewyn "price of salt is scandal"; received Yera's confidence about mill ledger; fell asleep in chair before fire caught
- **Elra Corrford**: spent evening sorting old letters by candlelight; watched clouds, predicted rain wrongly; walked long way round to avoid muddy square; told Marald he looked tired
- **Marald Corrford**: asked about rain; confirmed looking tired
- **Rozek Stenenridge**: burned letter after reading; found work in Staveford, moved there, did not return; **CLAIM**: Luena followed him to Staveford within the month
- **Tatho Brackick**: rode out of Kelford; by next market day living in Ravenmere
- **Volia and Kadrek**: talked of weather, harvest, lame horse
- **Kadrek Brackick**: argued with carter over price of sack of oats
- **Fenelle**: read almanac aloud, mispronouncing half the saints

**Environmental backdrop**: Ruts and puddles after thaw; crooked sun chalked on forge wall; smoke lay flat over fields; baker's boy late, line at oven grew long; frost silvered hedges; bell for vespers rang thinly; children chased hoop; cart with turnips creaked past well; dog barked then went quiet; wind off water smelled of salt and tar; bees hummed in lavender behind parsonage; gulls quarreled over fish heads by steps; rain threatened but held off; open-air booths illuminated with candles in paper funnels lining from church to hostelry; citizens preparing for midnight mass; no stars visible

## Montfermeil Tavern Scene (Christmas Eve 1823)
- Number of men (carters, peddlers) seated drinking and smoking around four or five candles in public room
- Room resembled all drinking-shops: tables, pewter jugs, bottles, drinkers, smokers; little light, great noise
- Fashionable bourgeois objects: kaleidoscope and ribbed tin lamp
- Female Thénardier attending to supper roasting before clear fire; husband drinking with customers, talking politics
- Discussion topics: vines near Nanterre and Suresnes flourishing; grapes, juice, wine quality; Breton wheat grinding problems (contains tares, fennel, vetches, hempseed, fox-tail, pebbles); miller complaints about grain quality
- Éponine and Azelma's laughter audible from adjoining room; very young boy (born preceding winter, age three or less) crying persistently in dark; mother did not love him, called him "the result of the cold"; child continued shrieking when clamor became annoying

## Main Characters Status
- **Jean Valjean**: Dead (drowned November 17, 1823, at Toulon)
- **Fantine**: Dead (buried in pauper's grave, January 1823)
- **Cosette**: Suffering under Thénardier household at Montfermeil/Kelford, age 8
- **Napoleon Bonaparte**: Defeated, imprisoned at Saint Helena

## Themes
- Destiny/chance; divine intervention; human resilience against oppression
- Waterloo as historical hinge; war's moral paradox; marauding and plunder
- Mundane life indifferent to empires; daily tasks continue beneath grand narratives
- Mystery/obscurity: Boulatruelle's search; Valjean's suspicious chain-breaking ease; mill ledger rewritten; sealed letter; letters burned
- Hidden transgressions and buried truths
- Human courage in extremis: Valjean risking life for stranger; topman clinging to rope; child enduring suffering
- Immense force culminating in immense feebleness affords food for thought
- Poverty and exploitation: Cosette's servitude; water scarcity; Thénardiers' neglect of own children; exploitation as professional system
- Parasitic exploitation; commerce of suffering; hospitality as merchandise
